item.title: Could 49ers duo of DeForest Buckner and Nick Bosa unleash a Jeffery Simmons-like effect?
item.description: Niners defensive tackle DeForest Buckner (99) sacks Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins as 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa (97) moves in during the second half of an NFL divisional playoff football game at Levi's Stadium on Jan. 11, 2020. (Tony Avelar/Associated Press) On Sunday, six days after Bears' just-acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons had a transformative impact on Chicago's defense, San Francisco 49ers just-acquired defensive tackle DeForest Buckner will make his debut against the Raiders at Levi's Stadium. To be clear, Buckner is not in Simmons' class. That's reflected in the compensation their new teams gave up to get them. The 49ers dealt a fourth-round pick for Buckner, 32. The Bears traded two first-round selections for Simmons, 29. But after Simmons was a 60-minute menace in a 34-17 win at Seattle, Buckner will be part of a defensive line that will welcome back All-Pro pass rusher Nick Bosa , who has missed the past five games with a calf injury. That is, could Buckner and Bosa, a duo with eight Pro Bowl selections between them, combine to have a Simmons-esque effect on the 49ers' defense? Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris is eager to find out. "To see these guys … for the first time this year," Morris said. "I think it'd be a lot of fun." Nick Bosa (97) and DeForest Buckner (99) celebrate Buckner's sack of quarterback Kirk Cousins in the fourth quarter as the San Francisco 49ers played the Minnesota Vikings in the NFC divisional round on Jan. 11, 2020, at Levi's Stadium. (Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle) Before last week's bye, the 49ers defensive front face-planted in a 29-20 loss at Atlanta on Oct. 25. After collecting nine sacks in their previous two games, the 49ers managed just three QB pressures, their fewest since Dec. 22, 2024. All-Pro linebacker Fred Warner said he was excited to play behind a line that will now include Buckner, Bosa and Osa Odighizuwa, who was acquired in an offseason trade with Dallas. "It helps when you have really talented players on the defensive line," Warner said. "It makes my job easier." The new-look line will face a challenge. Raiders QB Kirk Cousins isn't mobile, but the 15-year veteran's quick release is a major reason why Las Vegas has allowed 11 sacks, matching the fourth fewest in the NFL. Cousins cooking: At 38, surrounded by a less than stellar supporting cast, Cousins is continuing to show why Kyle Shanahan was eager to reunite with him when he became the 49ers head coach in 2017. Cousins ranks second in the NFL with 19 passing touchdowns, putting him on pace for a career-best 40. Cousins is third in passing yards (2,124) and seventh in passer rating (101.4). Morris isn't surprised by Cousins' late-career success. Morris spent the past two seasons as the Falcons head coach when Cousins made 22 starts for Atlanta. item.title: On Houston's transgender baseball team, nobody questions if I belong
item.description: A photo of me, at baseball practice, in October. (Mae Seeker/Courtesy) Standing beside a girl I met online and a friend from college, I looked down at the twenty three strangers gathered before me. These trans women, some young, some old, had come out on a brutally hot September morning in Houston, at a dusty little league field, to play baseball with me. There was a problem, though: I had never played baseball in my life. Inspired both by pickup baseball games started by transgender women around the country , colloquially known as "T-Girl baseball"; my adult guy friends who play sandlot baseball ; and my own love of America's Pastime, I took a stab in the dark. "Want to come play baseball with fellow trans women in Houston? Show up on Saturday," I posted on Instagram. I figured five or six people would pull up. Nearly two dozen came, some from Austin, others from as far as Dallas, with gloves and bats sourced from all over. Their wives, partners and friends came along with fans, tents for shade, first aid supplies and water and snacks. Getting people together to play baseball is not really in my nature. Outside of playing soccer briefly as a kid, I didn't play organized team sports. I insisted that I wasn't interested, but the truth is that at that age, I did not belong in my body. Gender dysphoria feels different to everyone. I've often compared it to brain fog, or feeling like your head is full of TV static. Every time I was asked to run the mile, all the times I was picked last and when I had to change in a locker room with boys, I was reminded that I was growing into a body I did not want. I buried those feelings and told myself sports weren't for me. It was only in college when I transitioned that I learned how to exercise, how to stretch and feel at harmony with myself, how to be at peace with the idea that I could try and fail at something. I now had the body I wanted, that I deserved. It was time to take care of it. In 2024, I was invited to play softball with some coworkers. It was embarrassing-I'd never swung a bat or fielded a ball. But it was also strangely addictive. Each time I played, I could feel myself getting a little better. When I finally hit the ball for the first time, it felt like mainlining adrenaline. It didn't matter that I grounded out, or that I was playing slow-pitch softball. I remembered thinking of Hall of Famer Ted Williams, who at various times called hitting a baseball the "hardest thing to do in sports." While it wasn't quite the same, I had done what I had once found impossible: I had tried a sport and improved. Joining a work sports team for fun is hardly abnormal, but as a trans woman in Texas, it felt like a quiet act of revolution. It wasn't lost on me that I was learning to love my body through sport as others like me were losing the ability to do just that. item.title: Battling a rare knee condition, Klein Collins' Brody Powers keeps fighting to play football
item.description: Klein Collins junior Brody Powers is seen on the sideline before a high school football game at Klein Memorial Stadium in Spring, Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) When Brody Powers puts on his football pads, he feels invincible. There's something about the game that invigorates him with an unmatched joy and energy. "I just love the feeling of football," Powers said. "Whenever I get to play it and put on the pads, I feel like I have superpowers. I feel like I can do anything." Long before he could wear pads of his own, Powers was wearing a football helmet and baby cleats in his car seat. His mother, Jennifer Powers, still has the pictures. The youngest of four boys, Brody grew up watching his brothers excel on the football field in high school while their dad, Steve Powers, coached. He dreamt of following in their footsteps, but that hasn't gone to plan. Brody's love for the sport started at an early age, but football has been snatched away from him on multiple occasions due to an uncommon knee condition. The disappointment has been difficult to cope with, and there have been times when simply bending his knee brought him to tears. Powers, a junior at Klein Collins High School, has been diagnosed with osteochondritis dissecans (OCD). It's a condition that damages the bone and cartilage inside a joint. The Pediatric Orthopedic Society of North America reports about 22 new cases involving the knee per 100,000 adolescents each year. The exact cause of OCD is not fully known, but doctors believe it develops from a combination of mechanical and biological factors that cut off the blood supply to the bone, according to the Mayo Clinic. The pain that Powers has battled during his journey with surgeries and intense physical therapy has been compounded by years of watching others enjoy the opportunities he desperately wanted for himself. "I'd say the hardest part is watching all my friends play football and have fun playing it while I have to sit on the sidelines and deal with this injury and recover from it," said Powers, who is now 16 years old. "That's been really tough. It just wasn't fun, especially when I was on crutches for four months while they were in football." Football has always been a huge part of life for the Powers family. (Courtesy of Powers Family) Football is a major part of life for the Powers family. Steve is the defensive coordinator at Klein Collins, and Brody's older brother Colby Powers - once a star quarterback for the program - is an assistant coach for the Tigers. His other older brothers, Landon and Bryson, also played football and had successful high school careers. Colby and Bryson eventually wound up playing together at the University of Tulsa. Brody, the youngest of the bunch by eight years, has always been in the stands or on the sidelines supporting his family through all of it. item.title: ‘It’s shocking’: Dean Wade says he has never seen anyone do what LeBron James keeps doing
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images LeBron James has won the respect of everyone inside the Philadelphia 76ers locker room. The 41-year-old is one of the greatest basketball players of all time, so the admiration and respect for the past were always going to be there. But he still had to live up to the hype, and it looks like he has done exactly that. Every 76ers player who has spoken about James has waxed lyrical about him. Dean Wade is the latest to join that group. Dean Wade hails ‘unbelievable’ Philadelphia 76ers teammate LeBron James Wade is in his eighth season in the NBA and has played with and against some great players over the years. The 29-year-old got the opportunity to share the locker room with James this season, and he seems to be learning a lot from the veteran. What has impressed Wade the most about James, however, is his basketball IQ, which allows him to be prepared for situations before they even happen. He said, as per Adam Aaronson on X : “His IQ is otherworldly. I’ve never met a person that has a higher basketball IQ than him… “It’s shocking how he can sniff out a play before they even get set. It’s unbelievable. I’ve never seen anything like it. He’s just an unbelievable teammate and just an unselfish player. “The way he passes the ball, the things he sees on the court, is unbelievable. It really is like – it doesn’t feel real.” Wade made those comments before the Philadelphia 76ers took on the Cleveland Cavaliers, where all eyes were on James on his return. However, The King, much like his teammates, was nowhere near his best on Friday night and deservedly ended up on the losing side. It now remains to be seen how James and his fellow Sixers will bounce back when they face the Chicago Bulls on Sunday night. item.title: Warriors' Georges Niang making mark by talking smack, drawing elbows and more
item.description: Warriors forward Georges Niang drives toward the basket against Miami Heat forward Bobby Portis and center Bam Adebayo on Thursday at Chase Center. (Yalonda M. James/S.F. Chronicle) The capillaries under Georges Niang's eye have been angry for a week. On Sunday they screamed when Niang caught an elbow to the socket from sinewy Los Angeles Clippers forward Derrick Jones Jr. The next day they turned the Golden State Warriors forward's lower eyelid black. By Friday, a watercolor of yellow and green shaded above his cheek, the skin healing and almost ready for the next bruise. There will be a next one. It is inevitable, the way the 33-year-old Niang plays basketball. On Thursday night, an already black-eyed Niang rammed his chest into the chest of Miami Heat big man Bobby Portis, then rammed his face into Portis' face. Sounds almost romantic. It was not. Portis' large body was impeding Niang's path back downcourt, as he saw it, and Niang has long built a lunch-pail identity on the same doctrine endorsed by Warriors teammate Draymond Green . He is not about to change, now, in Golden State. "When you think you're too good to take out the trash every single day, that's when you run into problems, right?" Niang told the Chronicle on Friday, a day after drawing double technicals with Portis in the Warriors' 120-100 win over Miami. "And I feel like my mentality of showing up, working hard, and being that chip-on-the-shoulder guy is - taking out the trash every day. Like, that's who I am. That's what's gotten me here. So why would I get here and then revert back to being, like, a nonchalant guy?" In all respects, really, Niang is one of the least nonchalant guys in the NBA. Against the Lakers last week, he went nose-to-nose and forehead-to-forehead with former Utah Jazz teammate Collin Sexton, for some reason. The Chronicle has gone around Golden State's locker room asking teammates for their favorite early-season Niang trash-talking moments, and most cannot give one. Not because they can't identify any but because they can point to too many. "He talks s- everywhere, bro," guard Brandon Williams said with a smile. "Yeah, everywhere. If it's something competitive, he's talking s-." One Warrior referred to Niang as a "walking clip." Reserve big Charles Bassey, who had Niang as a teammate in Philadelphia, said Niang - whose father is from Senegal - imitates Bassey's Nigerian accent every time he sees him (not, to be clear, in a bad context). Niang has cracked jokes about his own decidedly-un-NBA-like body while changing, and has donned a Jackie Moon costume from the movie "Semi-Pro" for Halloween, and sometimes "blacks out" when he gets to butting heads on the court, as guard De'Anthony Melton said. For all these reasons, and several sets of deeper intangibles, a veteran journeyman on a partially guaranteed minimum deal has glued himself across the cracks in Golden State's six-game winning streak. Niang has stuck, in coach Steve Kerr 's rotation and his heart.

item.description: Matt Rhule Nebraska © IMAGN Last month, the Nebraska Cornhuskers finalized a deal with quarterback Anthony Colandrea to return in 2027 for his final year of eligibility. He joined Matt Rhule and his team this year and took over as the team’s starting quarterback. Colandrea started the season with a bang, leading the program to a five-game winning streak. However, the team has struggled in the past few games. After Friday’s 24-13 loss to the Illinois Fighting Illini, the Cornhuskers are on a four-game losing streak. Yahoo Sports College Football reporter Dan Wolken shared his thoughts on Colandrea’s future with the program after this game. “Nebraska’s offense can’t continue like this, and yet they just re-signed the quarterback, which is the kind of thing you do when you believe it can continue like this,” Wolken tweeted. After a fan responded to his tweet defending the quarterback, Dan Wolken explained his reasoning and also questioned the program’s recruitment process. “He’s a good quarterback,” Wolken said. “The point is, you probably should fire the coordinator at this point given the results. But then you’ve got to go get a new one who runs a system specifically for the QB you’ve paid millions to but will only be there one more year. It’s not a great process.” According to On3 , Colandrea initially had a reported NIL valuation of $2 to $2.5 million when he first arrived at Nebraska. His new deal is expected to hike his valuation when he returns next year. With the senior quarterback’s return guaranteed after the signing, Matt Rhule can use him as a weapon in his recruiting process for 2027 by enticing portal talents and returning players. Before Friday’s game, Anthony Colandrea put up 1,825 passing yards and 15 TDs for the Nebraska Cornhuskers. Against Illinois, he completed 32 of 43 passes for 284 yards and a touchdown. Matt Rhule and his team are now 5-4 and haven’t won a game since defeating Maryland on Oct. 3. Before joining the Cornhuskers, Colandrea spent last season with UNLV. item.title: Man City Starting XI vs Nottingham Forest: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
item.description: Man City Starting XI vs Nottingham Forest: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup Man City Predicted XI vs Nottingham Forest as Enzo Maresca Sticks With Donnarumma Manchester City have a goalkeeper issue. Enzo Maresca does not appear interested in turning it into a goalkeeper debate. After Gianluigi Donnarumma’s latest mistake in the 3-2 win over RB Leipzig, the obvious question was whether Geronimo Rulli had done enough to force a change. The answer, plainly, looks like no. Maresca is expected to keep Donnarumma in goal for the Premier League trip to Nottingham Forest. The error was familiar, a shot at the near post, a goalkeeper beaten when he should not be. That is the problem with elite goalkeepers. One mistake becomes the story. Maresca, however, is taking a more functional view. He said: “It’s good overall. It’s good. It’s quite relaxed in terms of he recognised that, you know, he has done some mistake, but at the same time, as I said after the last game, also he has made some, some good saves.” He added: “So it’s just a matter of balance, try to avoid mistake and continue to do the right things.” Predicted Man City XI This is where selection gets straightforward. Maresca rotated in Europe, now he is likely to go back to the side he trusts most. Ruben Dias should return in central defence, with Abdukodir Khusanov the likeliest player to drop out. Photo IMAGO Phil Foden was given an opportunity on the left against Leipzig and did little with it. Jeremy Doku replaced him after the hour and looks set to start at the City Ground. item.title: Fermin Lopez talks Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo competition, losses to PSG and Real Madrid: ‘He’s the best’
item.description: Fermin Lopez talks Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo competition, losses to PSG and Real Madrid: ‘He’s the best’ In an interview with Mundo Deportivo , Barcelona midfielder Fermin Lopez hailed teammate Lamine Yamal as the best player in the world. The 23-year-old La Masia graduate, who recently made his 150th appearance for Barcelona in the win against Aston Villa, also discussed the competition for places in the team, particularly with Dani Olmo, while also opening up about the team’s recent form. On partnership with Lamine Yamal and Olmo It was pointed out to Fermin during the interview that Lamine, in a recent media appearance, had revealed that he enjoyed playing with the 23-year-old star due to the connection they share on the pitch. Elaborating on the said connection, Fermin explained: “It means a lot because for me he’s the best, and the fact that he feels comfortable with me as a player, and that we have that rapport and connection, is important to me and to the team. “I’ve known Lamine since we were kids, and when you have a friend off the field, you have that rapport too, and it’s even easier on the field. You know each other perfectly, and I think he and I know each other one hundred percent. “That’s what we try to do on the field, and I’m very happy to play with him because, honestly, he’s the best.” Lamine and Fermin share an excellent partnership. (Photo by Burak Kara/Getty Images) Fermin has had to share time with Olmo in the attacking midfield position under Hansi Flick, and the academy graduate relishes the challenge and competition. “It’s a really good competition because he’s a very good player, and in the end, we both try to make the most of our opportunities and do what’s best for ourselves. But we get along really well off the field; it’s a very healthy competition,” he said. “Ultimately, we’re teammates, and we get along well with each other, even when the other isn’t playing. The competition makes us better every day, and I think that’s important.” On team’s form and recent losses After enjoying a scintillating start to the season, winning 11 games in 11, Barcelona fell to back-to-back defeats against PSG and Real Madrid. Since then, the Catalans have managed to bounce back with victories over Alaves and Aston Villa. But ahead of tomorrow’s clash against Atletico Madrid there remain some lingering doubts about the team’s ability and performances against the big teams. Talking about what happened to the team leading to the Clasico defeat, Fermin explained: “I think what happened to us is that we weren’t sharp. We weren’t playing the way we had been, and that’s why people probably thought we were going to win by a landslide. Obviously, we didn’t, because it’s Real Madrid and they can beat you in any match. “We weren’t good, and everything went perfectly for them. Their first goal is what it is, and you’re already playing against the current in a match where you’re not comfortable with the ball, and everything becomes more difficult.”

item.title: ‘Never meet your idols’ – Angel Reese fan interaction at LSU divides fans
item.description: Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images A viral clip of Angel Reese is making the rounds on social media. Angel Reese made it clear she’s tapping the brakes this offseason, stepping away from the non-stop media circus to properly rest up and recharge. Still, she couldn’t say no to a trip back to where it all started. Reese rolled into Baton Rouge for an LSU game, sitting right by the floor before jumping on the broadcast to call the action and hitting the postgame press conference alongside Kim Mulkey. She might be keeping her calendar pretty light these days, but when LSU calls, the Bayou Barbie is always going to show up. Angel Reese responds to fan asking for their Chicago Sky jersey to be signed A clip made the rounds online showing Angel Reese signing autographs at LSU, and fans couldn’t help but laugh at her deadpan face the second someone slid a Chicago Sky jersey in front of her. She looked like she wanted to be anywhere else the moment she saw the jersey, even keeping a straight face and giving a cold response of “you gotta get a new jersey, boo.” Fans were mixed online, with some defending Reese and others not liking her response. This supporter started: “They say never meet your idols.” “Nice way to treat your fans.” Another said One supporter said: “Ungrateful.” “She was just taking a dig at Chicago Sky. item.title: My dream is to win Ballon d'Or - Gabriel
item.description: Gabriel played against Atletico Madrid on Manchester United's pre-season tour [Getty Images] Manchester United forward JJ Gabriel says his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or", as he closes in on a move to Real Madrid. The 16-year-old is still registered at United but has been training on his own in Spain after walking out on the club and relocating with his family. He has subsequently reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid but no deal has been signed as yet. On Friday, following one of his sessions, the teenager was approached by Spanish news outlet Marca who presented him with a copy of their newspaper, which featured a front-page story about his expected move to Los Blancos. The newspaper reported he told them in English: "My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or." United would be due compensation should Gabriel leave, although the figure will be lower if he signs for a club outside the Premier League. Though no club-to-club talks have been held, sources have told BBC Sport that Real have verbally agreed a deal with Gabriel and his representatives. Despite United having Gabriel's registration domestically, it is not thought it could prevent the youngster joining a club overseas as he now has a European Union passport through his mother, who has Cypriot origin. While Real and United are both in the Uefa Youth League this season, competition rules prevent players from appearing for more than one club in a single season and Gabriel scored a hat-trick in his final appearance for United against Sabah in September. He was named the Premier League's Under-18 player of the season last term, despite being only 14 when the season began. item.title: MotoGP rider fears Qatar airport closure as final race goes ahead amid safety concerns
item.description: MotoGP rider Francesco Bagnaia has revealed his fears about a potential Doha airport closure as the final round of the season goes ahead this weekend in Qatar . Safety concerns surrounding the current conflict in the Middle East have overshadowed this weekend’s final round in Lusail. Japanese team Yamaha have withdrawn from the event, ruling out four riders and leaving 18 on the grid. The majority of MotoGP media are not in attendance, either. Teams were reportedly sent emergency shelter locations and safety protocols on Thursday, including guidelines such as “move to cover right away”, avoid lifts in hotels and not to “touch or photograph any debris.” Francesco Bagnaia is worried about an airport closure (Getty) A total of 19 riders, out of 22 on the grid, had made it known that they did not want to travel to Qatar – and Italian rider Bagnaia has publicised his biggest concern. “I expected the atmosphere in the paddock to be like a normal weekend because there’s nothing… I feel that here we don’t have to be afraid of a bombing,” he said. “The only fear we might have is that they’ll close the airport. But I trust them, and I want to continue to do so.” Championship leader Marc Marquez , in an awkward press conference on Thursday in which just one question was asked about the safety fears due to the lack of media on-site, admitted he will leave Qatar on the “earliest flight possible” after the race. “I mean, I would like to be in another place,” he said. Marc Marquez can become a 10-time world champion (Reuters) “For that reason, I arrived on the latest flight possible, and I will leave on the earliest flight possible. But we are here, we are ready to race, and with full concentration.” Nine-time world champion Marquez can wrap up the title if he outscores Jorge Martin by 30 points and Marco Bezzecchi by eight points across the two races. The event takes place just three weeks before F1 is scheduled to race its penultimate round at the same circuit just outside of Doha. The F1 season is scheduled to end in Abu Dhabi on 6 December. A final call is expected to be made on the Middle East races by Tuesday, with the back-up of a one-off round in Imola.

item.title: MotoGP Qatar Grand Prix: Marco Bezzecchi storms to pole ahead of Marc Marquez
item.description: Motorsport photo Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi laid down a marker in qualifying for the Qatar Grand Prix, shattering the lap record to win a pole duel with Ducati's Marc Marquez . Bezzecchi's team-mate Jorge Martin , who is also Marc's nearest championship challenger, had a disappointing session, however, and will only line up 11th on the grid. Read Also: Jorge Martin targets first two rows at Qatar GP: 'I can manage the race with painkillers' With the four Yamahas missing after their withdrawal from this event, it was a much quieter circuit than usual in Q1. Around the long Losail lap, it would take a real stroke of bad luck for a rider to hit a yellow flag. There were in any case no incidents to disrupt the session, making it as pure a contest as one could wish for in temperatures of 34 degrees. Making a rare appearance in Q1 following his disastrous Friday, Pedro Acosta hit the ground running after seemingly finding something in the preceding Free Practice 2 session. He hit the top of the timesheets immediately, leading Fermin Aldeguer by over three tenths of a second after the first round of hot laps. The two Murcians swapped positions in the final phase of the session, however, with Aldeguer getting his time down to a 1m50.876s. He was already parked in the box by the time Acosta had whittled his down to a 1m51.087s. As it happened, Acosta's earlier time would have been enough to keep him ahead of Franco Morbidelli and the rest of those hoping to make it into Q2. The busier track in Q2 immediately produced what Q1 hadn't - a crash and a yellow flag. It was South Africa's Brad Binder who dropped his bike, his second spill of the weekend. Marc Marquez, Ducati Team Marc Marquez, Ducati Team Marquez dodged the yellow to register a record lap of 1m50.361s, but some of his competitors hit the danger area and had to wait a lap before trying to respond. It was Bezzecchi who really caught the eye when he did so, yanking the bar a few notches higher with a 1m50.065s, pulling out almost three tenths on Marquez. As the riders returned to the pits for one last soft rear tyre, the only other man within half a second of Bezzecchi was Trackhouse Aprilia's Raul Fernandez. That set up a grandstand battle in the final minutes of the session, with Marquez and Bezzecchi giving it their all. Marquez improved his time to a 1m50.294s, a cracking lap in itself but still no threat to Bezzecchi. The factory Ducati rider was happy enough with his effort, however, and called off his challenge confident that he would probably remain in the middle of the front row. That's exactly how it played out. Bezzecchi shaved a further fraction of time off with his final effort, but there was no real need as Marquez would remain his nearest challenger. Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) grabbed third on the grid on one of his favourite circuits. item.description: Aaron Judge - New York Yankees | © Imagn New York Yankees sportscaster Michael Kay faced a wild trade proposal involving captain Aaron Judge and Chicago Cubs NL MVP favorite Pete Crow-Armstrong. On Thursday’s Michael Kay Show, a caller named Tony from Dobbs Ferry suggested a hypothetical trade sending Judge to the Cubs for PCA, shortstop Nico Hoerner, and Japanese ace Shota Imanaga. Kay respectfully declined the hypothetical trade for obvious reasons. “First of all, I don’t think that the Cubs would offer that for Judge,” Kay said. “I mean, you have the guy who’s going to win the National League MVP. Nico Hoerner is a beast, and Imanaga is a pretty good pitcher. So I don’t think that they would offer that… I would have to say I would have to respectfully decline. I cannot trade the face of my franchise. I can’t, even if the deal makes total sense. I absolutely cannot do it… Sometimes things are bigger than, you know, what makes sense on a chart. Things are bigger. I can’t trade Aaron Judge. I can’t have my fan base revolt.” The caller added that the trade is meant to free up payroll tied to Judge’s nine-year, $360 million contract , allowing the Yankees to go after Tarik Skubal in free agency. However, Kay still declined. “But I don’t need starting pitching,” Kay continued. “Skubal is terrific. He’s a great pitcher who’s also had three elbow surgeries. He’s terrific, two Cy Young Awards, I love him, but I don’t need him. That’s not what the Yankees need. It should be good enough to have Cam Schlittler up top, and Cole and Fried and Rodón. They don’t need another starting pitcher.” Kay added that trading Judge out of New York wouldn’t earn the franchise any favor with fans. Moreover, even from Chicago’s side, the deal makes “no sense” because they’ll be trading for a soon-to-be 35-year-old outfielder. Yankees Get Good News on Aaron Judge’s Rehab Aaron Judge ended up missing the entire postseason after struggling with a calf strain late in the regular season. The Yankees won their Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox, but were swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. There was a chance Judge could feature in the ALCS in limited capacity had the Yankees gone through. In the latest Yankees’ injury report , the club expects the captain to be ready for 2027 Spring Training. The report said the Yankees outfielder has a moderate-grade strain of the soleus muscle in his right calf. Moreover, he is scheduled to visit Dr. Gregory Pearl for his rib injury he sustained early in the season. This is an encouraging update for the Yankees, who were unsure how to use Judge in the postseason despite the injury. While that never came to pass, opinions were divided on whether the Yankees would play Judge despite the injury , given the severity of his calf strain. item.title: Ponga-inspired New Zealand reach World Cup final
item.description: Kalyn Ponga featured with a protective arm guard for New Zealand [Getty Images] New Zealand (12) 34 Tries: Nikora, Gagai, McLean, Hughes, Willison, Nicoll-Klokstad Goals: Isaako 5 Tonga (10) 10 Tries: Fifita 2 Goals: Katoa Just 23 days after breaking his arm, Kalyn Ponga returned to inspire New Zealand to a 34-10 victory in a pulsating encounter with Tonga as they reached their first World Cup final since 2013. Ponga had been named initially in reserve and then as one of the interchange players in the build-up to this contest - and the expectation was that he would be eased back into action and play a limited role. Instead, head coach Stacey Jones stunned many with his decision to include Ponga in New Zealand's starting 13 but was repaid in full as the Newcastle Knights talisman starred on home turf at the McDonald Jones Stadium, in New South Wales, Ponga's impact from full-back was almost immediate as he sent Briton Nikora over in the right corner inside four minutes. He was also involved in the Kiwis' second try of the game - as his contest with his opposite number Lehi Hopoate was crucial to Dane Gagai grounding the ball. And while the swirling wind made conditions almost unplayable at times, he repeatedly gathered high kicks and made several telling defensive contributions. One of those included throwing himself in the way of Tonga's juggernaut second row Demitric Vaimauga to prevent a certain try, while his ability to stall Hopoate's run and prevent him from offloading to Isaiya Katoa stopped another at a key stage with New Zealand only 12-10 ahead. The prelude to this fixture was almost every bit as gripping as the main event. Tonga's traditional war dance, the Sipi Tau, was met by New Zealand's Haka and a long stand-off between the players provided the perfect backdrop to a contest brimming with athleticism, power and superb ball-handling skills. For the second week running, Tonga fans turned out in force with the stands a sea of red. And they witnessed their side's participation in a wonderful advert for rugby league with Jojo Fifita scoring two excellent tries. However, the match ultimately swung away from them in a five-minute period after the break when New Zealand's outstanding centre Casey McLean surged over in the left corner and the wily Jahrome Hughes darted in to score. On this occasion, Kristian Woolf's team, who effectively torpedoed England's hopes of reaching the last four with a 30-12 in their opening match on 17 October, were unable to stage the same sort of fightback that helped them defeat their Pacific Island rivals Samoa last weekend. With the scoreboard, time and a gale-force wind against Tonga, Xavier Willison punished them further when they failed to gather a short drop out. And when Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad superbly grounded Erin Clark's kick, it put the gloss on a fine New Zealand performance. item.description: Kimi Antonelli can’t see himself anywhere but Mercedes for now, but he isn’t ruling out Ferrari after Bernie Ecclestone predicted he’ll switch one day. Already, when he landed an F1 seat, the chatter grew that Antonelli would one day drive for Ferrari. A top Italian driver racing for the ultimate Italian team feels like a story written in the stars. For a long time, Ferrari has tried to get an Italian in its car. They got Giancarlo Fisichella back in the day and were preparing the likes of Antonio Giovinazzi and Antonio Fuoco for the ultimate switch, but it didn’t work out in the end. Both are still part of the Ferrari family in sports cars. But there is no doubt that Ferrari would keep an eye on Antonelli, even though they have the likes of Oliver Bearman and even Rafael Camara in their ranks as F1 juniors. Image Credit: James Sutton/LAT Images Ecclestone: ‘Kimi’s Heart Beats Italian’ For now, they are satisfied with Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, but there is growing tension among them. With Antonelli now the F1 champion, his stock has gone up considerably, and the Italian pull is still there. Former F1 boss Bernie Ecclestone believes he will drive for Ferrari one day, for Italy. “Ferrari has no choice, they have to do it,” he told F1-Insider . “And Kimi’s heart beats Italian. If he continues to win, and I’m convinced he will, he’ll switch to Ferrari out of love for his country.” Even Piero Ferrari has kept the door open for Antonelli , even comparing him to Niki Lauda. His son reportedly wants an Italian in the team too. But does the newly crowned champion want it? He isn’t ruling it out. Antonelli Doesn’t Rule Out a Ferrari Move Image Credit: Clive Mason/Getty Images For now, it is all Mercedes for him, naturally. But in the future, who knows? “I wouldn’t see myself anywhere else but Mercedes, especially now,” said Antonelli in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport . “They signed me when I was 11, took a risk with me, and have always believed in me. “I’m incredibly happy with where I am, and I’m grateful for everything we’ve done together and will continue to do. They’ve become a second family to me, and I think I’ve really taken a big step this year when I realized the team accepted me for who I am. And then for the future, very far away, who knows. We’ll see,” he said.

item.title: Five takeaways from Norwich City's latest accounts
item.description: Although group turnover totalled £40.3m, the club recorded an operating loss before player trading - of £42.3m [Press Association] Norwich City Football Club has released its latest annual report, detailing the club's financial standing for the year until 30 June 2026. It shows the Canaries recorded an operating loss of £13.3m - despite making almost £46m in profit from selling players. Before taking player trading into account, the club recorded an operating loss of £42.3m , compared with a £25.5m loss in 2025.​ While the Championship side reported increases in areas including attendances, retail and sponsorship, its operating costs also rose sharply. Here are five key takeaways from the club's latest annual report. Rising operating costs Staff costs have increased at Norwich City [Press Association] According to the report, the club's operating costs rose to £99.8m, from £79.2m the previous year. Norwich City said this reflected its "continued investment in the playing squad and football operations". A large chunk of this figure is staff costs, which rose from £48.1m the previous year to £57.9m in 2026. These costs included wages, National Insurance, pensions and other employment costs. Within that figure, wages and salaries rose from £39.9m to £49.6m. Profit from selling players Norwich City striker Josh Sargent completed a move to Toronto FC in a deal worth more than £20m [Press Association] Norwich City did record significant profit from player sales. The departure of players such as Borja Sainz, Jonathan Rowe and Josh Sargent helped earn the club £45.9m profit from player trading, up from the £24.3m achieved in the previous year. The accounts also included £16.8m in player amortisation, an accounting process that spreads the transfer fees paid for players over the lengths of their contracts. After player trading was taken into account, the club's operating loss fell from £42.3m to £13.3m, which it said was "broadly consistent with the prior year's result". In the report the club said: "Player trading remains an important part of our financial model and generated profits of £45.9 million during the year, helping to offset underlying operating losses." Fan support remains strong Fan support has remained strong with a slight increase in shirt sales [Press Association] The average attendance at Norwich City's Carrow Road stadium was 25,899, while the club sold 20,039 season tickets. The club described this as "another strong year" for ticket sales. Retail revenue increased to £2.4m, helped by an 8.6% increase in replica shirt sales, with more than 29,000 shirts sold during the season. The report said figures showed "the incredible loyalty and commitment of our fanbase." Investment in the squad During this period the club has signed new players such as Mathias Kvistgaarden [Press Association] Norwich City has invested heavily in signing new players, with the accounting value of its player registrations rising from £32.6m to £53.9m. item.title: ‘Make sure you smile’: Rutgers coach Steve Pikiell continues to preach positivity amid cancer battle
item.description: Rutgers coach Steve Pikiell was on campus the day before his team’s season opener against New Haven, and he sent a message to acting head coach Brandin Knight hours before tipoff. “It’s funny, he said, ‘Make sure you smile,’” Knight recalled following the Scarlet Knights’ 81-54 victory at Jersey Mike’s Arena . “That was one of his big things, like have fun, enjoy it. It’s always about the guys but have a good time and smile. That’s the way he is. He can find some positivity in anything. Pikiell, 58, announced that he was battling cancer in September, and Knight, the 44-year-old who was brought on Pikiell’s staff in 2016 and had been his associate head coach the previous five seasons, was tabbed as acting head coach. While Pikiell focuses on his health, Knight draws inspiration from his boss, who contributes his time and thoughts where and when he can as he cycles through treatments and rests. “Coach is one of the strongest people I know,” Knight said. “He’s showing up here two or three times. He is showing how tough he is. It’s not easy to get out of bed and do things like that, but he comes around. He’ll sit and watch practice. He’ll give encouraging words.” Pikiell was not among the spectators at Jersey Mike’s Arena, but support for his fight was evident throughout the crowd with students and fans wearing red T-shirts emblazoned with “ Rutgers Tough ” across the chest. They were selling for $30, with 100 percent of proceeds going to RWJ Barnabas Health’s efforts in cancer treatment and patient care as part of a fundraiser envisioned by Pikiell. A video of former players like Caleb McConnell, Dylan Harper , Ace Bailey and Ron Harper Jr. talking about different examples of being “Rutgers Tough”played on the scoreboard above center court. Knight noted that the shirts sold out in the first day. Players will continue to wear them during warmups this season. item.title: Cam Newton shares the only way Shedeur Sanders can become the Browns’ starting QB
item.description: Photo by Al Pereira/Getty Images Shedeur Sanders has been named as the starting quarterback for the Cleveland Browns this weekend as they face the New Orleans Saints. Todd Monken confirmed on Friday that it would be Sanders taking the starting role for the Browns, with Deshaun Watson working his way through the concussion protocol following the recent loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Sunday will mark the first start of the season for Sanders, who has been forced to watch from the sideline after Watson won the job over the offseason. However, the controversial young quarterback now has the opportunity to prove himself under Monken in a game situation. Given the impressive season Watson has enjoyed so far for the Browns, former NFL quarterback Cam Newton has laid out exactly what it would take for Sanders to make the starting role his own. Cam Newton sets target for Shedeur Sanders in battle against Deshaun Watson So far this season, Sanders has only thrown three passes across two games in the NFL. The 24-year-old completed both of his passes last weekend when he came into the game against the Steelers, and he has shown his confidence ahead of the game against the Saints. “The only way I see Shedeur Sanders starting for the rest of the season if they exceed any type of benchmark that was set like if I think it was like 300 yards plus,” said Newton on his YouTube channel. “If they have a 400-yard offensive day, oh man, we got to reconsider some stuff.” The chances of that happening against the Saints may not be as unlikely as Newton may think, though. The New Orleans Saints’ defense has allowed 372 yards of total offense per game on average this season. However, even with Watson at quarterback, the Saints have only managed to average 301 yards of total offense per game this season. So, sealing a 400-yard game with Sanders at quarterback would certainly be something. item.title: Leverkusen squad mentality under fire as Martinez calls on squad to "clear our heads"
item.description: Leverkusen squad mentality under fire as Martinez calls on squad to "clear our heads" After a recent dip in form, the signals some of the Bayer Leverkusen professionals are sending reportedly points towards attitude issues. As reported by Kicker.de this afternoon, the body language in the camp does not suggest that of a “defiant response” to adversity. Aleix García’s regret — rather than immediately pressing to recover — following his error that led to Marseille’s opening goal, is one example. Additionally, Malik Tillman’s behavior at half-time is yet another concern for the Rhineland club when analyzing the teams mentality. While the other five substitutes passed the ball among themselves, the American “stood on the sideline, juggling the ball five or six times.” Thereafter, Tillman was pictured “resting his right foot on top of the ball to watch his teammates” rather than warm up himself. “We need to clear our heads. We need to improve mentally," coach Carles Martinez said in today's press conference to face 1.FC Köln. "Especially when it comes to sticking together and working as a team, to be competitive. We need to break this run of poor results.”
